metadata.original_query: Search the web and use reliable sources. Find the latest publicly quoted USD/INR, EUR/INR and GBP/INR exchange rates. Show the quote timestamps and explain briefly how reference rates differ from rates a traveler receives. Return only the answer in Markdown with source citations. Keep the complete answer within approximately 100-500 tokens; aim for 150-220 words including headings and citations. Avoid a generic introduction and follow-up offers. If requested current data is unavailable, say so briefly.

## Reference rates vs traveler rates
Reference rates are benchmark or indicative market rates used for pricing and valuation, while travelers usually receive a worse rate because providers add a spread, fees, and sometimes cash handling or card conversion charges. ECB and NSE publish reference-style rates, and Reuters notes its market quote data can be delayed, which also distinguishes it from the final retail rate a traveler pays. [12][3]
